subject: Request: Escrow credit + flexible ramp language for Brightline renewal
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: escrow credit + flexible ramp language for Brightline renewal

Sanjay —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our conversation, Brightline’s main sticking points for the renewal are: early termination exposure during the 6-month ramp and the need for a clear downsell path if usage doesn't meet forecast. You asked for two concrete items we could consider to proceed:

1) A refundable escrow credit that protects Brightline from having to pay full committed fees if they substantially underutilize in months 1–6.
2) A ramp schedule with explicit downsell thresholds and an opt-out window tied to usage and mutual notice.

Attached is a short SOW revision (Brightline_SOW_v3.pdf) and a spreadsheet with a sample escrow calculation (proposed_ramp_credit_calc.xlsx). High level proposal:

- Escrow credit = 30% of first-quarter committed spend held in account; refundable pro rata for demonstrated underutilization after month 6, or converted to future credits on retention.
- Ramp schedule: Month 1 = 20% commit, Month 2 = 40%, Month 3–6 = linear build to 100%.
- Downsell protection: If trailing 30-day usage < 60% of committed baseline at any ramp checkpoint, Brightline may request downsell to a lower tier with a 45-day transition notice; a one-time transition fee equal to 10% of monthly committed MRR applies.

If this general structure works for procurement/legal, we’ll need an executive approval for a one-off escrow arrangement and the 10% transition fee concession. I’m looping Lauren and Marcus to validate the finance and commercial impacts.

Next steps I propose: you confirm acceptance of the structure; we route to our Deal Desk for an exception; if approved, I’ll get the SOW revision into DocuSign.

Thanks —

Dev Patel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0189

Attachments: Brightline_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW revision stub), proposed_ramp_credit_calc.xlsx (pricing model stub)

From: Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: escrow credit + flexible ramp language for Brightline renewal

Dev —

Appreciate the fast follow. A few clarifying questions from procurement/legal before we escalate: 

- Can you confirm the escrow will be refundable on a pro rata basis tied to usage (not subject to arbitrary holdbacks)? We need a simple reconciliation formula tied to token/usage logs.
- We need to avoid any language that creates an ongoing credit liability on your balance sheet longer than 12 months. Can the refund be converted to service credits only (no cash refund) unless there is material failure to deliver?
- The 10% transition fee looks reasonable, but procurement prefers a cap (e.g., not to exceed $25k) to avoid unexpected overage charges on smaller tiers.

Also, legal would like the opt-out window to be triggered only after independent third-party usage metrics are reconciled and not earlier than 120 days post-go-live.

If you can get internal signoff on a refundable-credit-to-credits conversion with a 12-month cap and a $25k transition-fee ceiling, we can move quickly.

—Procurement (on behalf of Brightline)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 12:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: escrow credit + flexible ramp language for Brightline renewal

Team —

Forwarding Brightline's asks. Quick read: procurement wants (A) escrow refundable to service credits by default (cash only on material performance failure), (B) 12-month cap on credit liability, (C) $25k cap on transition fee, (D) opt-out only after 120 days + reconciled metrics.

My take: we can approve a credits-first escrow (helps our cash/stats) and a $25k cap on transition fee. The 12-month cap is reasonable but we need to tie the refund conversion mechanics to our existing billing and trials flow — Engineering/Platform should be able to produce the usage log export by customer. Monica, can legal draft language that limits cash refunds to "material failure to deliver" and specifies the reconciliation formula? Marcus, run the P&L impact using the attached spreadsheet and confirm worst-case exposure under the 12-month liability cap.

We should treat this as a Deal Desk exception for DL-2026-089 and route this to Finance for final signoff. I don't think we need VP-level signoff unless exposure > $500k.

If everyone agrees, Dev please confirm acceptance to Brightline with the revisions: credits-first escrow, 12-month liability cap, $25k transition fee cap, opt-out earliest at day 120 post-go-live subject to reconciled usage.

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: escrow credit + flexible ramp language for Brightline renewal

Sanjay / Procurement —

Thanks for the clear feedback. We can accept the credits-first escrow model with the following guardrails (per internal review):

- Credits-first escrow: escrow converted to service credits by default. Cash refund only after a material failure to deliver, defined as failure to meet 3 of 4 SLO categories (availability, throughput, security controls, or severity 1 incident response) where failure is attributable to Redwood. Legal will draft the exact clause.
- 12-month maximum liability window for escrow credits. Any unused credits after 12 months expire.
- Transition fee cap: $25,000 maximum. For very small tiers, fee will be the lesser of the calculated 10% of MRR or $25k.
- Opt-out window: earliest request allowed after day 120 post-go-live; final effective downsell requires 45 days' mutual notice and reconciled usage (our exported logs will be the source of truth; we will provide the CSV for reconciliation).

Lauren has approved this as a Deal Desk exception for DL-2026-089 and Marcus will confirm P&L impact by EOD. Monica will circulate proposed contract language for your legal review.

If that aligns, we’ll prepare the SOW revision for signature and the DocuSign link.

Action items: 
- Marcus Lin: P&L exposure calc; confirm under $500k threshold?
- Monica Patel: draft clause for credits-first escrow and material failure definition
- Dev (me): prepare updated SOW in DocuSign once internal signoff is done

Appreciate the partnership —

Dev Patel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
